title: VPC Concierge Approval Flow PRD (raw)
content:
Context / Why this exists:
We ship Private deployments where customers bring their own VPCs and manage much of edge networking. That introduces operational friction: changes to NAT/egress, gateway rules, or routing can block onboarding or trigger audits. Currently we have ad-hoc email/Slack approvals + manual evidence collection. This doc sketches a productized "Concierge" approval flow that balances minimal audit evidence, operator ergonomics, and customer control.

Problem statement (short):
- Customers need a low-friction path to make small networking changes during onboarding and maintenance while preserving an auditable trail and separation of duties.
- Operators must be able to triage and approve/reject changes quickly without losing forensics or introducing broad permissions.
- Audit/Compliance teams require compact, verifiable evidence bundles for changes that impact data egress or connectivity.

Product goals (measurable):
1) Reduce median time-to-approve for routine VPC onboarding changes from ~8 hours to <45 minutes (by Q2 pilot).
2) Ensure every approved change produces a compact evidence bundle that satisfies SOC-style spot audits (fields documented below).
3) Provide an operator UX that surfaces risk score and rollback guidance; target TTR (time-to-recover) < 15 minutes for common rollback paths.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full policy engine for customer ACLs. We won’t attempt to model customer-specific firewall semantics at first pass.
- Not intended to replace long-lived change management for infra-wide revisions (we focus on onboarding and low-risk tweaks).

Core concept: "Concierge Approval Flow"
- A lightweight approval orchestration service that mediates change requests between Customer Operator (CO) and Redwood Operator (RO).
- Customer submits a structured Request (JSON template or UI) describing intent (egress exception, NAT mapping, port open).
- The system computes: risk_score, minimal evidence checklist, required approvers (role-based), and suggested fallback (e.g., ephemeral rule with TTL).
- RO can approve, request more evidence, or trigger a safe rollback path. All actions produce signed, timestamped audit receipts.

Minimum required fields on Request (template):
- request_id (UUID)
- customer_account_id
- operator_contact (email/ID)
- intent_type (egress, nat, port_open, route_update)
- justification (free text, encouraged to include ticket id)
- ttl_seconds (optional; preferred for ephemeral exceptions)
- change_patch (diff or CIDR/rule spec)
- customer_signature (optional: SAML assertion / signed JWT)

Audit evidence bundle (compact):
- request_id
- request_payload (canonicalized JSON)
evidence_schema: (stringified list) [timestamp, actor_id, action, pre_state_hash, post_state_hash, operator_signature, customer_signature(optional), supporting_links]
flows:
User journeys (sketch):
1) Simple ephemeral egress (happy path): Customer UI -> select external destination -> set TTL (1h) -> Concierge computes low risk -> autosuggest: ephemeral NAT + egress rule -> RO auto-approve policy triggers (if matches policy) -> change applied -> bundle archived -> notification to customer and ops.
2) High-risk route change (escalation): Request contains route update that matches sensitive prefix -> risk_score high -> Concierge requires 2 RO approvers + compliance acknowledgement -> request lands in RO queue with annotated playbook -> one approver requests more evidence -> CO uploads syslog snippet + infra ticket -> after approval, change applied with canary rollout + continuous monitor job -> bundle stored in immutable ledger for 1 year.

Operator UI needs (quick list):
- Compact summary panel: request_id, customer, intent, TTL, risk_score, suggested rollback, links to ticket + prior similar requests.
- Inline diff viewer for change_patch with pre/post state snapshots.
- Approve / Request more info / Reject / Escalate buttons (all actions 1-click).
- Ability to attach operator notes and select rollback playbook.

Approval policy primitives (first iteration):
- auto_approve_rules: pattern-based allow-lists (e.g., egress to cloud-storage.* for backups)
- ttl_enforcement: ephemeral only if ttl <= 3600 seconds and destination not on deny list
- approver_count: mapping from risk_score bucket -> required approvers (0..2)
telemetry_and_observability:
Metrics to emit: request_latency_ms, approvals_per_hour, avg_risk_score, time_to_approve_by_bucket, rollback_invocations, false_positivees_detected_by_monitoring. Logs: structured audit events emitted to customer and Redwood SIEM, with retention policy configurable per-account. Dashboards: per-customer approval volume, mean approval duration, top requested intents. Traces: link to API call, orchestration steps, and applied API to underlying network agent.

Retention and compliance knobs:
- Evidence bundles archived in S3-like store with immutable write-once semantics (WORM) for configurable retention windows (default 365d).
- Mini-archive for low-risk ephemeral events: keep canonical bundle + checksum but redact payloads after 30d to reduce storage.

Security model / signing: 
- All operator actions signed with Redwood HSM-backed keys; customers may optionally provide their own signing key to append to bundles.
- Proof-of-approval contains pre_state_hash and post_state_hash computed from canonical rule set; this enables verification during audit without shipping full config blobs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Concierge accepts structured requests via UI and API and returns deterministic risk_score.
- Auto-approve rules can be configured by product/ops and applied to live queues.
- Evidence bundle schema generated for every approved change and retrievable via API with proper RBAC.
- Operator UI with approve/request-more-info/reject workflows, and audit receipts for each action.

Rollout Plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal): limited to SRE & Solutions Eng; instrument 50 synthetic requests; validate telemetry and evidence bundles. 2–4 weeks.
- Pilot: enable on 3 low-risk customer accounts with opt-in; collect operator feedback and iterate UI and risk calibration. 6–8 weeks.
- GA: expose to broader set of customers, add tenant-level retention config, and integrate with contract SLA paths.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to compute risk_score deterministically and reproducibly? Proposed: rule-based scoring + ML model second-pass later.
- Integration points: customer KMS for optional signature — legal review required.
- What data counts as "supporting evidence" for SOC auditors? Need to align with Security & Compliance.
- Rollback automation surface: do we run reversal scripts or revert to prior config snapshot? Need SRE input.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Operators over-rely on auto-approve rules -> too permissive. Mitigation: conservative defaults, rate-limited auto-approvals, post-hoc sampling review.
- Risk: Evidence bundles grow too large -> storage costs. Mitigation: compact schema, state hashes, configurable redaction windows.

Next steps (concrete):
- Priya: draft API contract for request/response (open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/210) — due 2025-01-24.
- Ethan: prototype risk scoring rules + example rule set (first draft) — due 2025-01-30.
- Marta: schedule 1:1 with Security to confirm evidence fields required for audits — due 2025-01-22.
- Samir: mock Operator UI flows (Figma) and a clickable prototype — due 2025-02-07.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally rough. Focus feedback on the evidence schema tradeoffs (compactness vs. fidelity), policy primitives we should expose to customers, and how strongly we should guard auto-approve defaults.

References / inspiration: examples from other managed infra change workflows (cloud db maintenance, network ACL exception systems), and internal runbooks (see linked artifacts).

End of draft.
